source.org_or_authors: A. K. Dokania and P. Kruit (TU Delft)
source.quote: The values of shear modulus from our samples were obtained by fitting the straight line to the curves in Fig. 4, which shows the values of 0.5 (500 000 N/m2), 0.64, and 0.635 MPa for 95, 142, and 190 um of the RTV 566 thickness, respectively.

gaps: No source found of beryllium faces bonded to aluminium honeycomb (or any Be-to-higher-CTE structure) through an elastomer interlayer. The only beryllium-specific adhesive statement opened is NASA Ames/Arizona 1990 (SIRTF), which says a classic bonded mount with silicone-type adhesives is not feasible for beryllium and uses flexures instead.
No Materion design guide on bonding beryllium found or opened.

No measured shear modulus for NuSil CV-2566 or CV-2289: only DMA storage modulus E' for CV-2566 (4.0 GPa below Tg, 0.004 GPa above, frequency and temperature of the 'final' reading not printed). Shear modulus near 1.3 MPa would be an inference (PROJECTION, not recorded as a row).
Current Avantor-hosted CV-2566 data sheet not retrievable (HTTP 522); values come from the 2014 Rev A and 2018/2023 republished sheets, which disagree on lap shear (500 vs 575 psi).
RTV 567: nothing found. Sylgard 184: no lap shear, no outgassing, no density other than specific gravity on the Dow Corning sheet. DOWSIL 93-500: no modulus printed.

3M 2216 B/A Gray: lap shear strength is not printed in the extracted 3M sheets (only 3200 psi via the Huie table); the 'Shear Modulus' values (342 MPa at RT) carry a suspect label and are identical across Gray/Translucent/Tan sheets.
Hysol EA 9361 data sheet not obtained; the EA 9360 bulletin (a stiff toughened epoxy) is recorded only for contrast.

Truly soft polyurethanes (Solithane 113, Uralane/Arathane 5753, Lord) not read: only filled Appli-Thane 7300 and 3M DP6310NS/DP6330NS (hundreds of MPa) were opened. Lord and Hysol polyurethane data not found.

No face-sheet / honeycomb-core specific thermal shear formula was found. The formulas recorded (Bayar family, Yoder, Daly and Hawk via Huie) are for a lens or disc bonded in a cell; applying them to a laminate is an extrapolation (PROJECTION). Chen and Nelson 1979 (thermal stress in bonded joints) is cited by NASA Glenn but not opened.

Outgassing, creep and modulus at cryogenic temperature for the elastomers (relevant if the beryllium structure is cooled) are mostly missing; only CV-2566 Tg -125 C and the 2216 and Milbond modulus-versus-temperature rises are on record.
